name: Bartosz Ciechanowski — GPS
oneLine: Long-form GPS explainer where every paragraph hands off to a draggable, hand-built WebGL figure; prose-first, zero chrome.

palette.note: Off-white page behind the 700px text column and most figures
Body copy; headings a touch lighter at #535353
Full-bleed black band for the opening 3D satellite-constellation canvas
Inline color-keyed nouns (e.g. 'landmark') matching the figure's blue marker
Gold for the draggable figurine and orbit paths; red #E92525 and green carry other keyed objects
Saturated blue masthead band only (sampled from screenshot)

type.note: 19.2px / ~1.6 line-height, weight 400, ~65-70 char measure; keyed terms switch to weight 500 + color
H1 44.8px and H2 28.8px, weight 500-600, gray #535353, sentence case, tight default tracking
Masthead wordmark ~48px semibold white on blue; figure scale/labels small 11-14px

layout: Single centered ~700px column at 1440px; figures break out to ~700-1000px or go full-bleed (the black constellation band) with ~120px vertical air above and below.
Strict rhythm: 2-5 short paragraphs, then one figure, repeated across ~12 H2 sections (Simple Positioning, Time of Flight, Orbits...). 62 canvases on one page.
Paired figures: 3D isometric scene on the left, flat 2D map on the right in a thin bordered card, so one manipulation reads in two projections.
motion: Figures are live WebGL scenes, not videos: the opening globe shows real satellite orbits rendered as thin gold ellipses around a textured Earth.
(inferred) Satellites animate continuously along orbits and many figures carry play/scrub sliders that step through time; nothing animates on scroll, motion is user-driven.
(inferred) Dragging rotates the camera with damped inertia; drag-able objects (yellow figurine) update linked circles/maps in real time at 60fps.
interactions: Drag-to-orbit camera on 3D scenes; drag the yellow figurine to move position and watch distance circles redraw.
Color-keyed prose: the word 'landmark' in blue maps to the blue dot in the figure, acting as a legend inside the sentence.
(inferred) Inline range sliders under figures scrub time / parameters.
steal: Hero: open the telemetry site with one full-bleed black band containing a draggable 3D orbit of the ESA spacecraft, thin gold orbit line, no UI chrome.
Method section: color-key prose to plots, e.g. 'nominal' in one color and 'anomaly' in another, with exactly those colors in the adjacent time-series chart so text doubles as legend.
Results walkthrough: the paragraph-then-figure rhythm with paired views (raw multichannel signal left, model's latent/anomaly score right) linked to one shared scrubber.
leave: The blog masthead (saturated blue band, social icons) reads as a personal blog, not a SpaceX/Apple-grade product page.
Light #F8F8F8 body with gray headings is too soft for our dark, high-contrast space direction; keep the rhythm, not the skin.
